### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `439ecf3e1c4fd93b401eefa07c4c206716957146` — the merge of head `e7f2dd03933e75164c156918ab9b4a8a60e7b4f6` into base `92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 439ecf3e1c4fd93b401eefa07c4c206716957146 && git checkout 439ecf3e1c4fd93b401eefa07c4c206716957146
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175 e7f2dd03933e75164c156918ab9b4a8a60e7b4f6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175 && git merge --no-ff e7f2dd03933e75164c156918ab9b4a8a60e7b4f6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Reviewed: PR #24688 (draft, base `92ce3af404a9b6ca16881a89f2e841d29da52175`, 11 files, +530/-1, three commits), card #24625, the seat's measured record 6278938192, the claim 6278944518, the dev's os-dev-report 6279731318, PR #24587 (merged) and PR #24681 (draft). Every file:line below is read on the head tree `e7f2dd039` unless another tree is named. The diff touches no governed surface (the file list carries none of the register's paths). Principals are named by class; no credential, link or body value is written here.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Every door is closed for a principal without `manage_platform_settings` — judged door by door, both logs.**

The mechanism is one declaration, field `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']` on `body_text` and `body_html` (sys-email.object.ts:116-128, sys-identity-email.object.ts:120-132). The security plugin folds a field whose capabilities the caller does not all hold into a non-readable, non-editable field-permission entry (security-plugin.ts:9338-9341, ADR-0066 D3), the FieldMasker then deletes the key from every served row (field-masker.ts:85, :184, :237), and the same fold is the engine's one answer to "may this caller filter, sort, group or aggregate by this field" (security-plugin.ts:9381-9383, `getQueryableFields`). So:

- `/data` list, get, query, and `select=` projection: the key is dropped, never masked-in-place; a body predicate is refused. Pinned on the 18.0 fixture for the organization administrator at dogfood :145-159 (list, both rows, no body key), :161-168 (get by id and get with the body named in `select`), :170-178 (query by id without body; body `$contains` probe 403); platform-admin control :180-189. Correct.
- Body filters: refused by the queryable-fields answer above; pinned :176-177, control :186-188. Correct.
- Global search: `searchAll` (metadata-protocol protocol.ts:15839) asks the security service `getQueryableFields(object, context)` per object per caller and hands the engine only that subset (protocol.ts:15920-15936; engine.ts:2037 states the same contract), so a body term is never scanned for this reader and the sweep stays 200. The pinyin companion never takes a `requiredPermissions` field as a source (search-companion.ts:134-137). Pinned :196-202 (member and organization administrator: 200, no hit, no echo), control :204-208. Correct. Observation, not a defect: the matrix carries no positive control that the organization administrator's subject-term search still hits `sys_email`; the queryable-subset path says it does, so the changeset's "does not match on a body" is accurate as written.
- Body as group key or aggregate input: `count()` and `aggregate()` run the middleware chain only, with the AST on the operation context (the engine's own prescription at engine.ts:3358: a hook-shaped filter would not narrow a total or a group, the middleware seam does), and both share the one search expander (`expandSearchOnOptions` at engine.ts:20225 and :20368 into :14066), so the fold's `readable: false` refuses the body in `groupBy`, `aggregations`, `having` and `orderBy` exactly as in `where`. Not probed by the new matrix; closed by the same gate that closes the filter.
- `sys_activity` and `sys_audit_log` mirrors, read side: the redaction serves a mirror only the parent fields the security service serves this reader (`resolveServedFields`, activity-field-redaction.ts:20-24 and :38; audit-log-field-redaction.ts:24 and :70), so the 18.0 copy is served to the organization administrator without the body; the #21154 guard (parent-field-query-guard.ts:36-42, installed ahead of the read gate at audit-plugin.ts:501-504) refuses a value-column predicate to a reader withheld any field of the parent, pinned or not. Pinned :215-219 (rows served, no body span), :221-228 (probe 403, parent named and unnamed), :230-233 (member, no body), control :235-240 (platform administrator reads the 18.0 copy). Correct.
- Export: `GET /data/:object/export` (data-action-routes.ts:911) passes `enforceApiAccess('export')` then the user-level `enforceExportPermission` (:937), and projects through `security.getReadableFields(objectName, context)` (:1172), so a caller who is admitted at all never receives the body columns. The seat's matrix measured the organization administrator refused outright on `main`. Not re-probed by the new matrix; closed twice by existing gates.
- Views and related lists: both are served through `/data` with the caller's context; no second projection exists. Closed by the data door.
- REST `history` route: the route ledger carries only the metadata history route (rest-route-ledger.ts:262); a record's history is `sys_audit_log`, covered above.
- Realtime / change feed: the engine publishes the full record body (in-memory-realtime-adapter.ts:87-92) to server-internal subscribers only; no client transport is wired, pinned as `realtime-delivery-authz` (authz-conformance.matrix.ts:453, state experimental). Not a principal door today; a pre-existing latent surface, outside this card.
- Analytics query: cube members are admitted through the security service's `getReadableFields` (field-read-admission.ts:28-29), so the body is neither a group key nor an aggregate input there.
- MCP bridge: fails closed on every `sys_*` object (runtime/domains/mcp.ts:748).
- plugin-email's own routes: none serve rows; the plugin registers only its manifest (email-plugin.ts:396 on `main`). The pipeline reads as the system and is not narrowed (changeset :19), which is the intended carve-out.
- Attachments: `attachments_json` (sys-email.object.ts:191) is not gated; it carries attachment metadata and inline attachment content, never the body, and identity mail carries no attachments. Residual nil.
- `sys_identity_email`: object-level `requiredPermissions` (sys-identity-email.object.ts:46) plus the new field gates; pinned :272-276 (organization administrator and member 403), control :278-282.

Door the matrix missed: none found that is open. Doors named above but not probed by the new test: export, aggregate/group-by, analytics; each is closed by an existing gate that the diff does not touch.

**2. The field-level choice versus the claim's wish (organization administrators keep their own non-identity bodies).**

The dev measured that `sys_email` has no reliable identity-row selector. PR #24681 does define one for the ceremony (organization-ownership-apply.ts:3351-3377 on `dceaa5646`): `related_object = 'sys_user'`, OR `related_object IS NULL AND related_id IS NULL` AND a body that carries better-auth's magic-link sign-in path. Judgment: the dev is right for a READ gate. That selector is raw SQL evaluated once by a migration; the security layer has no declarable row policy over body content (`requiredPermissions` is object- or field-level, RLS predicates do not read a column's text), and its magic-link arm is a content heuristic. A false negative in a move leaves a row behind, which this PR's field gate still covers; a false negative in a read gate is a served reset link. So the only selector that is reliable for a gate is "every row", which is the field-level answer. The narrowing is the correct interim fix for a p1 credential exposure, and the changeset states it as before / now / unchanged / why / remedy (changeset :17-22), naming that the organization's own notification and invitation bodies are lost and that the row's envelope, subject, state and linkage stay.

The dev's proposal B (relax the `sys_email` body gate once the ceremony has moved identity rows out) is NOT safe on the step 6 guard alone, for two reasons the seat should hold against any relaxation PR:
- The ledger keeps pre-fix copies. `sys_audit_log` rows written before this fix about 18.0 identity rows keep `object_name = 'sys_email'` and the body in clear in `old_value` / `new_value`. The ceremony re-points `sys_activity` only (organization-ownership-apply.ts:3451-3456 on `dceaa5646`) and its PR body says the audit log is a ledger and is not rewritten. The ledger redaction serves a copy the fields the data plane serves for the parent (audit-log-field-redaction.ts:24, :70), so relaxing the `sys_email` body gate re-opens those copies to the organization administrator.
- The magic-link arm is heuristic: an 18.0 magic-link row rendered from a customized template without the default sign-in path stays in `sys_email`.
Conditions for B: (a) a cleanup that masks the body columns of pre-fix `sys_audit_log` and `sys_activity` copies at rest (precedent: `os migrate audit-metadata-bodies`, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-metadata-bodies.ts), (b) a measured census of residual rows with no related object after the ceremony, and (c) its own Clause-② widening changeset. Until then A stands.

**3. The mirrors' masking (plugin-audit).** `ledgerView` masks both body columns of a mail-log row to the read mask (SECRET_MASK), preserving null (audit-writers.ts:1758-1762), after the credential mask (:1729-1735) and the internal-field omission (:1748-1750); the function is the one view taken for the create `new_value`, the delete `old_value`, both halves of an update diff, the activity row and the label source (its contract, the doc above :1722). The two names live once (mail-log-body.ts:22-30) and are re-exported from the `audit` barrel (index.ts:16); plugin-audit depends on `@objectstack/platform-objects` as a runtime dependency, so the import is publishable. Pinned: audit-internal-field-omission.test.ts:301-354 (all four snapshot sides, null preserved, non-mail-log control, activity ran), dogfood :284-293 (at rest, both logs, HEAD-written rows). Correct, and the same shape as the credential mask.

Pre-fix stored mirror rows: still hold bodies in clear at rest. They are served only to a reader served the body (the platform administrator reads the 18.0 copy: dogfood :235-240), so there is no escalation, but it is a credential copied at rest and the hazard in item 2 above. This is a residual. The dev assigns its carrier to #24581, yet #24681 (the #24581 PR) states it does not rewrite `sys_audit_log` and re-points `sys_activity` without masking. So the residual has no carrier in code: a cleanup card is owed (R2 below). The ceremony is the natural place (it already touches the activity rows of every moved mail), or a sibling `os migrate` command on the `audit-metadata-bodies` pattern.

**4. The `sys_approval_request` `searchableFields` change (outside the claimed surface).** On `main` the object declares no `searchableFields`, so the ADR-0061 auto-default applies (search-fields.ts:242-249, `autoDefaultFields` :127), and `textarea` is in the auto set (:52-53); `payload_json` is a `Field.textarea` (object :412), so it was scanned. The snapshot guard refuses any query naming `payload_json` to a reader withheld a field of ANY registered object when the query pins no subject (payload-predicate-guard.ts:38-47, :221-236). Once mail bodies are withheld from every organization administrator, that reader's `$search` on the object, and the global sweep passing through it, became 403: a shipped latent defect that this narrowing would have turned on for every tenant administrator. The fix declares the auto-default minus `payload_json` (object :83-96) and pins the derivation so a later textual field goes red rather than silently unsearched (search-fields.test.ts:19-26). Correct, minimal, pinned, and producer-side (PD #12) rather than a per-caller carve-out in the sweep. It changes results for everyone: free-text search no longer matches inside the JSON snapshot, the platform administrator included; a structured filter on the snapshot is unchanged for readers the guard admits. Both are stated in the changeset (:18) and the PR acceptance notes. `node_config_json` (textarea) stays searched; it is flow node configuration, not a record snapshot.

**5. Tests.** The matrix file counts 22 cases: data API 6, global search 3, mirrors 8, identity log and writers 5. Platform-admin controls at :180-189, :204-208, :235-240, :278-282 make every "absent" a gate, not an empty fixture. The organization-admin non-body control is :145-159 (subject and status served for the identity row AND the organization's own invitation). No body, link or token value appears in a title, message or log: probes compare a span read as the system by inclusion and report a boolean (:71-77). The "9 red on unchanged `main`" reading and ablations A1-A3 are the dev's (Local-runs none): A1's 8 red is the matrix minus the two writer pins, consistent; A2's void preflight is disclosed and the dist reach shown by the dogfood red; A3's 1 unit + 1 dogfood red matches item 4. Unit pins: mail-log-body.test.ts:26-38 (both logs gate exactly the two body columns; `sys_email` keeps no object-level gate). The sibling equality pin (sys-identity-email.object.test.ts:16 on `main`, `fields` toEqual) holds because both objects received the identical declaration. Gaps, none blocking: no export probe (closed by two existing gates, measured 403 on `main` by the seat); no positive subject-search control for the organization administrator; the get-by-id probe accepts either 200-without-key or 403 (:165-166), both closed. The file declares no measured budget while booting a real stack; that is the lane's debt under the suite-weight rule, not this PR's blocker.

**6. The 18.x line rule R1-R4 on the merged tree.** Dev-reported on `e7f2dd039`: R1 fresh showcase boot and sign-in with 200 answers, no error lines, server stopped; R2 the harness with five neighbours, 6 files, 62 passed; R3 the v17 case still refused; R4 cli `serve-walled-posture-refusal`, 5 passed. The PR run's `Dogfood Regression Gate` completed in 11 s with its three shards skipped, so the harness did not run in CI on this head; it runs on `main`'s push and hourly battery. Under Local-runs none these stand as reported, not re-verified.

**7. Interaction with PR #24681 (head `dceaa5646`).** File overlap: zero (set intersection of the two file lists is empty). Neither PR's code assumes the other: #24681's 5b note says nothing on `sys_email` changes and the exposure is neither widened nor fixed there; this PR touches no ceremony file. One test premise does interact: the new matrix boots the raw 18.0 fixture through `bootFixture`, which composes `OrganizationOwnershipBootGuardPlugin` (populate-fixture.ts:63-71). On #24681 that guard refuses an 18.0 database without the ceremony, no escape hatch (its guard header :63-64 on `dceaa5646`), and its harness asserts exactly that refusal through the same `bootFixture` (upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts:81, :141-159 on `dceaa5646`). So whichever of the two lands second will red `identity-mail-read-gate`'s `beforeAll` on the merged tree. Prescription for the second lander (R1 below): run the ceremony on the fixture copy first, as the harness's 1b does, then restate the matrix: the moved 18.0 identity rows are probed in `sys_identity_email` (object gate), the organization-invitation row keeps the `sys_email` body-gate probes, and the pre-fix `sys_audit_log` copies with `object_name = 'sys_email'` keep the mirror probes (the `sys_activity` copies will have been re-pointed to the sibling).

**8. Semver, Clause-② and the changeset.** `minor` for `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` (changeset :2-4), BREAKING flagged (:13) under the launch-window convention (check-changeset-no-major.mjs header); the three are the packages whose published behaviour moves, so the grade is right and the level axis is discharged (`Check Changeset` success). `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` governs the fixed group only and is unaffected. Clause-② reads `yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset (:9). The gate reads the arm and carries the axis either way (check-changeset-no-major.mjs:1669-1676), and the narrowing arm is what sets this record's tier, so the tier is unaffected; but the reference spells a pure narrowing `no (narrowing)` (contract-review.md:12), this diff adds no key to any published payload, and the `main` corpus carries 168 `no (narrowing)` against 87 `yes (narrowing)`. Non-blocking spelling note (R3). ADR-0087 marker: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with the why (:11). Correct category: nothing is removed, renamed or re-shaped, the three packages publish, no id covers this behaviour, and the change is behavioural; the category's one refusal is a migration prescription in the body (check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:147-153), and the body's Remedy is an operator permission-set remedy, not a consumer rewrite. The changeset is complete: before / now / unchanged / why / remedy, and it names the approvals search change for every reader.

**9. CI check-runs on `e7f2dd039`, read at 2026-10-19T23:54Z (40 runs).** success: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (aggregator; shards skipped), `Lint · ESLint`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` lane, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, the four PR-protocol checks (card claims branch, no other PR claims the issue or the single-writer path, part-of does not close), `Auto Label`, `filter`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `(5/6)`, `(6/6)`. in_progress: `Test Core (2/6)`, `(3/6)`, `(4/6)`. skipped: `Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`. No failure. The required `Test Core` context was not yet complete at review time; landing precondition ② (all checks green) is the seat's re-read before readying and queueing.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on the three moved packages, declared BREAKING under the launch-window convention. Consistent with the changeset and with the narrowing: a published read accept set shrinks (two fields withheld from every non-platform reader on two objects; one object's free-text search set shrinks for every reader; the ledger copies of two objects mask two columns). No published schema, export, enum or stored shape changes; no ADR-0087 registration is owed. Clause-② arm: narrowing (spelling note R3).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (A accept field-level now, B relax after the ceremony): A accepted. B refused as proposed; it is admissible only under the three conditions in ①2 (ledger cleanup at rest, residual census, its own widening changeset).
- R1 — Serial constraint with #24681: whichever PR lands second must restate `identity-mail-read-gate.dogfood.test.ts` over a ceremonied fixture (①7). Not a defect of this diff on its base; the claim already binds the second lander to merge `main`. The seat should name this in the landing order.
- R2 — Residual, no carrier in code: pre-fix `sys_audit_log` and `sys_activity` copies of mail-log rows hold bodies in clear at rest, served only to readers served the body. The dev's carrier (#24581) does not carry it (#24681 does not rewrite the ledger). File a card: mask the body columns of pre-fix mirror copies at rest, ceremony step or `os migrate` sibling on the `audit-metadata-bodies` pattern; make it a stated precondition of any `sys_email` body-gate relaxation.
- R3 — Clause-② spelling: a pure narrowing with no new key is `no (narrowing)` per the reference; the gate and this record's tier read the arm, so the effect is nil. Correct on the next PR-body edit; the changeset line may follow in the same commit if one is made for other reasons.
- Pre-existing, out of scope, acknowledged: the 17.x backport is owed when `release/17.x` is cut (seat record 6278938192); the realtime fan-out is a latent server-internal surface already pinned experimental.
- Dogfood file declares no measured budget: lane debt under the suite-weight rule, not this PR's.
